title: Alt key conflict in Grab and Move with Powershell
author: ZL114514
summary: Grab and Move’s default Alt hook can withhold Alt from applications and Explorer during non-Grab mouse interactions, breaking PowerShell Alt+click and desktop Alt-drag semantics.

status.label: Modifier passthrough design ready
status.detail: Two reports show cross-application suppression and current hook code reveals deferred replay.

next_action.label: Design non-Grab Alt passthrough
next_action.reason: Delay or cancel Alt absorption so unrelated gestures receive native semantics while preserving window drag.

judgment.rationale: The updated issue broadens impact beyond one app, and the current modifier hook provides a specific design boundary.
evidence: A second reporter says desktop Alt-drag moves files instead of creating shortcuts.
Grab and Move defaults to Alt.
Current code can swallow bare Alt before a Grab gesture exists.
judgment.recommended_action: Continue focused input-state design and regression tests; keep approval gated until passthrough timing is proven.

issue_context.summary: Applications and Explorer do not receive Alt when needed because Grab and Move reserves it before knowing whether the user will move a window.
known_information: Both left and right Alt reproduce in PowerShell 7.6.3 on 0.100.2.
Expected PowerShell behavior is Alt+click for a split pane.
Desktop Alt-drag should create a shortcut rather than move the file.
No assignee or linked fix exists.
inferences: Replaying Alt on a later key or release may be too late for mouse controls inspecting modifier state during click/drop.
Deferring consumption until movement commits to Grab and Move may preserve native gestures.
issue_context.analysis: The second report proves a general passthrough defect rather than a PowerShell-specific request. Code inspection supports design without generic diagnostics.
initial_investigation: GrabAndMove/main.cpp defaults g_modifierKey to Alt and g_shouldAbsorbAlt to true.
KeyboardProc swallows Alt keydown and replays it later if no Grab consumes it.
#49121 improved modifier-click passthrough, but current code still defers Alt during unrelated mouse interactions.
Closed #47294/#47302 addressed Alt+Tab targets, not these timing cases.
